task.name: Sprint starting phase hides long pre-story/reuse gates behind identical gate log lines
task.story_text:
A sprint can spend many minutes running pre-story gates while `forge status` still reports the sprint as `starting` and all stories as `waiting`. The log emits repeated identical `Running gate: make forge-gate TEST_TARGET=.` lines for semantically different gates, so the operator cannot tell whether Forge is running the baseline gate, validating an existing stranded worktree for reuse/review, or validating active story work.

Expected behavior: status and logs should identify each gate's purpose, target story/worktree/base SHA, and current phase. Long pre-story/reuse gates should be visible in `forge status`, not hidden under top-level `starting` with stories shown as waiting.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `10fdbd8ae9d06ab628dc15da924fa691c0bcaefd` captured at `2026-07-28T21:56:41.137562+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/coordinator/gate.py` — `sha256:aba9097b35d79ec38e6eefa7f478cb68ce6fc242a93bcfa17e03c008568827d8`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/util.py` — `sha256:2bafe565cab1f05301e616cbd397708df22f5ed3fc04e7c476db615e1b38f4f2`
- `src/theforge/log_util.py` — `sha256:fd5e1109ae0be930c1d08dbd552edbbf25cf4413df54676b635ef94ecb6ef008`
- `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py` — `sha256:6c1ce1978f51ba06c009814c932d7da5791cf35a714de09574e8f0a9536c9d24`
- `src/theforge/sprint/dag.py` — `sha256:20db19b210310890e9154198c88752e301d61d80e0452921819cc7ee957ad222`
- `src/theforge/sprint/state_writer.py` — `sha256:9dcdd8b6c803ac6e815117bcf398fdac61d4ec4d7e8bf9dd47c51e163da3c580`
- `src/theforge/cli/sprint.py` — `sha256:ed70222681929d11634fcb303165be2873db9c629a6aab5cc560a070cdd3675f`

### Observed symptom

During sprint startup, Forge sequentially runs one gate subprocess per
story (a "reuse gate" validating whether an existing/stranded worktree is
still review-ready), plus one baseline gate on the sprint merge base. All
of these gates emit the identical log line
"Running gate: make forge-gate TEST_TARGET=." with no indication of which
gate is running (baseline vs. which story), how long it has been running,
or its purpose. Meanwhile `forge status` continues to report
sprint_phase: starting and every story's status/phase as waiting/null for
the entire duration of this loop — which can take many minutes to tens of
minutes per story (observed ~13 min for issue-50, indeterminate for
issue-230) — so the operator cannot tell Forge is doing real, potentially
slow work versus being stuck.

### Reproduction / evidence

Issue body's captured run c237211427ba (hforge sprint --issues 50,230
--parallel 1 --resume) shows three identical
"[forge] ... Running gate: make forge-gate TEST_TARGET=." lines
corresponding to (1) the baseline gate (~79s), (2) the issue-50 reuse gate
(~12m48s, resolved to "worktree exists, gate passes (5 commits ahead)"),
and (3) the in-progress issue-230 reuse gate. `hforge status --no-color`
during gate #3 still showed
"phase: starting" and "○ #50  waiting  —  waiting / ○ #230 waiting — waiting"
and the on-disk state.yaml showed sprint_phase: starting with both
stories at status: waiting, phase: null. This matches the code paths
identified below.

### Hypotheses tested

- **[confirmed]** The gate log line is a low-level shared logging call that doesn't receive per-call context (slug/purpose/worktree), so it can't distinguish baseline vs. reuse-gate vs. which story.
  - Evidence: src/theforge/coordinator/gate.py:109 logs `_cu._log_verbose(f"Running gate: {gate_cmd}")` — only the resolved shell command string is interpolated. run_gate_full() (gate.py) already computes `slug = task.slug if task is not None else "baseline"` internally (used only for {slug} template substitution in the gate command itself), and both call sites — the baseline call at sprint/runner.py:1108-1131 and the reuse-gate call inside _triage_spec at sprint/dag.py:655 — have slug/branch/worktree_path/purpose in scope at the call site but don't thread it into the log call. This is a plumbing gap, not a structural limitation.
- **[confirmed]** sprint_phase and per-story status/phase are never updated during the reuse-gate triage loop, so status necessarily shows starting/waiting for its entire duration regardless of logging fixes.
  - Evidence: Bootstrap seeds sprint_phase='starting' and each story status='waiting'/phase=None (sprint/state_writer.py write_bootstrap_state, ~lines 248-307). The sequential per-story reuse-gate triage loop (sprint/runner.py:2745-2758, calling _triage_spec -> _run_gate at sprint/dag.py:655) runs entirely before the first update_state_phase call, which only happens afterward at sprint/runner.py:2786-2791 (transitioning to 'intake-remediation'). Nothing inside the triage loop calls SprintStateWriter.update(...) for any story; the first per-story phase update (state_update_fn({'phase': 'STARTING'}) and set_worker_slug) happens later in _run_single_story (runner.py:~1620-1624), i.e. only once a story is actually dispatched into dev iteration, well after all reuse gates for all stories have already completed.
- **[ruled out]** Parallel simulator/host contention or CPU load explains the variable gate durations (79s vs 13min), i.e. this is a performance bug rather than an observability bug.
  - Evidence: Issue's own investigation used --parallel 1 (only one gate active at a time) and observed xcodebuild at ~0.1% CPU while the app/simulator progressed through async HealthKit test work — real wall time from slow test content, not host contention or a stuck process. This does not change the observability gap; it just explains why the fix boundary here is status/logging, not gate performance.

### Confirmed cause

Two compounding, independently-confirmed causes produce the reported
symptom:
(1) run_gate_full()'s single log call at coordinator/gate.py:109
(`_log_verbose(f"Running gate: {gate_cmd}")`) interpolates only the
resolved gate command string, never the slug/purpose/worktree context
that is already in scope at every call site (baseline call in
sprint/runner.py:~1108-1131; reuse-gate call via _triage_spec in
sprint/dag.py:~655) — so identical-looking gate invocations for
semantically different targets (baseline merge base vs. each story's
existing worktree) are logged with the exact same text.
(2) The sequential per-story reuse-gate triage loop in
sprint/runner.py (~2745-2791, calling into sprint/dag.py's
_triage_spec/_run_gate) runs entirely while sprint_phase remains
"starting" and before any per-story status/phase field is written;
sprint_phase only advances to "intake-remediation" after the entire
loop (all stories' reuse gates) completes, and per-story
status/phase fields stay at their bootstrap values ('waiting'/None)
until a story is later dispatched into _run_single_story — so
`forge status` has no per-story or per-phase signal to surface during
potentially very long reuse gates.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/coordinator/gate.py:~100-109 (run_gate_full — gate command
resolution and the unlabeled "Running gate: {gate_cmd}" log call)
src/theforge/sprint/dag.py:~509-534,~655 (_triage_spec — has slug/branch/
worktree_path in scope when calling _run_gate for reuse validation)
src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:~1108-1131 (baseline gate call site)
src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:~2745-2791 (sequential triage loop over all
stories; first update_state_phase call happens only after the loop)
src/theforge/sprint/state_writer.py:~248-307 (write_bootstrap_state —
seeds sprint_phase='starting', story status='waiting'/phase=None)

### Fix-success criterion

With --parallel 1 and at least one story whose existing worktree requires
a multi-minute reuse gate: (a) the sprint log distinguishes the baseline
gate from each story's reuse gate by including the gate's purpose and
target (e.g. "Running baseline gate on merge base <sha>: ..." vs.
"Running reuse gate for issue-50 on feat/issue-50 <sha>: ..."), and (b)
while a story's reuse gate is running, `forge status` (and state.yaml)
show that story in a concrete non-waiting phase (e.g. REUSE_GATE /
PREFLIGHT_GATE / VALIDATE_EXISTING) with elapsed time and worktree/branch/
commit identified, rather than sprint_phase: starting with all stories
status: waiting.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- Gate wall-time variance (79s vs ~13min) traced to genuinely slow async HealthKit simulator test content in the HDP adopter repo, not Forge-side contention or a stuck process — a test-content/performance concern for that repo, not a Forge observability bug.

### Notes

The reuse-gate triage loop (runner.py:2745-2758) is sequential per story
even though it iterates a dict of all stories — this ordering (all
reuse gates finish before sprint_phase leaves "starting") is confirmed
directly from code layout, not inferred. The fix must touch both the
logging call (gate.py) and the state-writer/phase-transition code
(dag.py's _triage_spec loop in runner.py + state_writer.py), since fixing
only the log text would leave `forge status` blind, and fixing only
status would leave the log lines ambiguous.
## Ruled-out / clarified hypotheses

This was not parallel iOS simulator contention: the run used `--parallel 1` and only one HDP gate was active.

This was not high host CPU load: `xcodebuild` was around 0.1% CPU while the test app/simulator advanced through async HealthKit window reads. The wall time was real, but the operator could not distinguish simulator wait time from Forge waiting/idling because status stayed at `starting`.

## Affected behavior

This affects sprint startup/triage/reuse validation observability, `status` state updates, and gate log labeling.

## Fix-success observable

While Forge is running a baseline gate, status should say baseline gate and include elapsed time. While Forge is validating an existing story worktree, status should show that story in a concrete phase such as `REUSE_GATE`, `PREFLIGHT_GATE`, or `VALIDATE_EXISTING`, with elapsed time and the worktree/branch/commit being gated. Logs should label gates with purpose and story, for example:

```text
Running baseline gate on merge base <sha>: make forge-gate TEST_TARGET=.
Running reuse gate for issue-50 on feat/issue-50 <sha>: make forge-gate TEST_TARGET=.
Running reuse gate for issue-230 on feat/issue-230 <sha>: make forge-gate TEST_TARGET=.
```

A long reuse gate should never leave `forge status` showing top-level `starting` with all stories `waiting`.

handoff.summary: Added gate identity and pre-story progress publishing. A new GateLabel pure-data type (coordinator/state.py) carries a gate's purpose, story slug, branch or baseline marker, commit, and worktree; run_gate_full/_run_gate accept it and render it in the single 'Running gate' log line, preserving the old text when unlabeled and never letting the label reach the shell command. The baseline gate call site labels its gate with the merge base and the runner publishes sprint_phase=baseline-gate with a detail string and started_at (cleared in a finally), then sprint_phase=triage across the reuse-gate loop; update_state_phase was extended with detail/started_at and the status header now renders 'phase: baseline-gate (merge base of main, 13m)'. _triage_spec builds the reuse GateLabel (branch tip SHA read from the git log output it already had) and brackets only the gate with optional on_gate_start/on_gate_end callbacks; the runner's callbacks write the story to the bootstrap state file via a new update_state_story helper as status=running / phase=REUSE_GATE with started_at, branch, commit, and worktree, reverting to waiting with that detail cleared when the gate returns. status_reader renders the REUSE_GATE phase as 'validating <branch> @ <commit>' with live elapsed time.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: While Forge is running a baseline gate, status says baseline gate and includes elapsed time
acceptance_criteria.notes: sprint_phase=baseline-gate with sprint_phase_detail='merge base of <base_branch>' and sprint_phase_started_at; header renders 'phase: baseline-gate (merge base of main, 13m)'. The exact merge-base SHA is in the log line rather than the header, since it is only computed inside _run_baseline_gate after the phase is published.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A long reuse gate never leaves forge status showing top-level starting with all stories waiting
acceptance_criteria.notes: The window is now sprint_phase=baseline-gate, then starting briefly, then triage during the reuse-gate loop, with the gated story non-waiting throughout its gate. sprint_phase=triage is published before the loop and the existing intake-remediation transition still fires after it.

story_deviations: Updated 21 _triage_spec stub signatures across 7 existing test files (added **_progress) because _triage_spec — the seam the story requires extending — gained keyword-only progress callbacks and MagicMock side_effect functions reject unknown kwargs. No assertions or test intent were changed. The alternative designs (an extra git rev-parse per story, or a phase covering the cheap git probes and omitting the commit) were less accurate against the AC.

The baseline phase detail names the base branch ('merge base of main') rather than the merge-base SHA, because the SHA is resolved inside _run_baseline_gate after the phase is published; the SHA is carried in the gate log line.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
